name: 90/90 Hamstring
setup: Set up with one leg long and the knee soft, toes pointing to the ceiling.
cues: Fold from the belt line toward the floor and stop at the first firm pull.
Breathe out long and let the floor come a little closer each exhale.
Keep the reach smooth: no bouncing at the end of the range.

faults.fault: Rounding down from the upper back to reach further
faults.fix: Reach your belt buckle toward the floor, not your nose.

faults.fault: Bouncing at the end of the range
faults.fix: Hold still at the first firm pull and breathe out.

name: Adductor/Groin
setup: Set up seated or lying on the floor with the working hip turned out and the other leg resting easy.
cues: Sit tall toward the ceiling, then hinge forward until you meet the first firm pull.
Breathe out long and let the floor take more of your weight.
Ease out of the stretch as slowly as you eased in.

faults.fault: Forcing the knee down with the hands
faults.fix: Let the floor do the work: hold still and breathe out.
Grow tall toward the ceiling first, then fold.

name: All Fours Quad Stretch
setup: Set up so the front of the hip and thigh can open: kneeling, side-lying or standing with a hand on a wall for balance.
cues: Tuck the belt buckle up toward your chin before you reach for more range.
Push the back knee gently toward the floor and hold still.
Let the air out long and stay at a firm pull, never a sharp one.

faults.fault: Arching the lower back to fake the range
faults.fix: Tuck the belt buckle up first; the range you keep is the real one.

faults.fault: Yanking the foot toward the seat
faults.fix: Ease the heel toward the seat over a slow count of three.

name: Ankle Circles
setup: Clear a few metres of floor; move through the drill at an easy pace first.
cues: Move smooth and slow at first, then let the range grow.
Breathe out long at the end of each reach.
Keep the rhythm steady, like a slow beat.

faults.fix: Slow the rhythm and own the end of each range.
Stop at the first firm pull; it opens over the set.

Hold still and breathe out long.
